messages.author: 2d85373b3089780a
messages.subject: TITAN and non-tumor data
parts:
The documentation clearly states that "TITAN is a tool for predicting subclonal copy number alterations (CNA) and loss of heterozygosity (LOH) from tumour whole genome sequencing data".

However, would you still recommend using TITAN for non-tumor data? Canvas is a similar tool for CNV detection with WGS data and they say that their tool can be used for non-tumor WGS data, although their documentation focuses on tumor data.

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: TITAN and non-tumor data
parts:
Hi,

TITAN can be used for datasets with some sort of pairing.  The "tumour" sample is really just the "sample-of-interest" and the "normal" is the reference sample. TITAN detects changes in copy number of the sample-of-interest relative to the reference.  There is also the consideration of whether you want total copy number or allelic copy number differences between the 2 samples.  TitanCNA is specifically designed to give you allelic copy number.  For total copy number only, you can use HMMcopy, which shares the same pre-processing steps as in TITAN.  The advantage of analyzing total copy number is that a reference sample is not strictly required.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Gavin
